note: PLACEHOLDER. Written to make the sweep exercisable end to end, not to test the agent. Nobody has driven one of these turns, so a verdict drawn from this list is a claim about the pipeline, not about the Chief of Staff. EIGHT cases, and DEFAULT_JUDGE_CONFIG.gates.minCases is 20. A corpus verdict over this list therefore resolves CAN'T SAY however the judge voted, because the floor was set from measured agent non-determinism and eight runs measure that rather than the branch. Eight is deliberate and not a rounding error: one clean baseline plus seven single-axis variations is what one change can author honestly across four chat agents. Whether to grow every list to 20 or to lower the floor is still open, so do not read the shortfall as a decision. WHAT THE HARNESS SEEDS for this scope (runners/seedChatOrg.ts): one organization with customPositionName 'Council Member' and an election-api positionId, and one electedOffice. No priorities, no briefings, no community issues, no contacts. THE CONSTITUENT-DATA PAIR IS OFF FOR A DEPLOYMENT REASON NOW, NOT A SEEDING ONE, and that is a correction to what this note used to say. The seeder sets organization.positionId, which was the one gate that lived in our own database: resolveByOrgSlug returns null on a missing positionId before it asks anything else, so districtFilters was null and the pair registered on no scope at all. Two gates it cannot set remain, and neither is a row anyone could seed. The position itself lives in election-api, which DistrictResolverService reads over HTTP, and query_constituent_data additionally needs a Databricks credential that the provider factory returns null without. Both are absent locally and in CI, so query_constituent_data and describe_constituent_data are still unregistered on every run this harness makes today — but they register the moment a credentialed deployment drives this same seed, which runners/seedChatOrg.tools.integration.test.ts proves against the real handler and the real resolver. So 'constituent-count' measures the capability gap here and becomes a data-path case wherever those two credentials exist; read its verdict as conditional on the environment rather than as a fixed property of the case. Four cases lean on an absence on purpose rather than by accident: 'priorities-on-file' reads an empty priorities table, 'constituent-count' asks for a tool this run does not carry, 'capability-inventory-from-context' asks the agent to describe exactly that, and 'action-the-agent-cannot-take' asks for something it cannot do at all. An empty priorities list and an unregistered constituent tool are the two states this agent meets most often in the wild, so measuring them is not settling for what was convenient. Varied along: a read of a seeded (empty) table against the product-knowledge map against a capability the agent lacks; one right answer against a judgement call; a turn that needs a tool call against one answerable from the system prompt and tool inventory alone; a well-formed request against a rambling multi-part one; and a turn the agent should decline or reframe. 'constituent-count' says 'registered voters' ON PURPOSE. It is the vocabulary probe: a Serve official who used a Win noun, and whether the agent reframes to constituents is exactly what the CoS golden bench grades as a cross-cutting criterion. Every other question here uses Serve vocabulary (constituents, office, term) per docs/product-vocabulary.md. Four questions are lifted from the Chief of Staff golden bench at src/chats/general/chief-of-staff/evals/cases (capability.yaml, privacy.yaml, input_robustness.yaml, grounding.yaml), which is where questions that have already discriminated live; the judge uses only a case's question and ignores its gold value, so that bench transplants cleanly. People are fictional placeholders in the house style (gp-webapp e2e-tests briefings.spec.ts uses 'Test Official'); this file is public, so no real person is named. States, cities and office titles are real.
